Question 3 integrated into FR-048, FR-049, FR-051, SC-012, Edge Cases, and Assumptions.

## Question 4 of up to 5

**Question:** When a read request carries the `X-Paste-Password` header more than once, with different values, which value should the service treat as the password being presented? (FR-058)

**Why it matters:** The Edge Cases section already has a bullet titled "An empty or repeated password header" but only explains the empty case — the repeated case is named and then left unanswered, so a test has nothing to assert. It also has a security edge: if the service silently honours a later copy, a caller could get a value accepted that an intermediary logging or inspecting the first copy never saw.

**Recommended:** Option A - It matches the stance the spec already takes for an empty header value (treated as a presented password that does not match rather than as absent), introduces no new error class — FR-070 reserves 400 for invalid option values — and guarantees no value can count that an inspector of the request would not have seen.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Treat a repeated header as a presented password that does not match, and refuse the read as forbidden (403). No single occurrence is ever selected. |
| B | First occurrence wins; later copies are ignored. (This is what naive header parsing usually yields, so it is the accidental default.) |
| C | Last occurrence wins; earlier copies are ignored. |
| D | Reject the request as invalid client input (400), treating a duplicated password header as a malformed request rather than a failed password check. |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (<=5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
